The test image shows two bell peppers with large, dark sunken lesions covering much of the fruit surface. The lesions show:
- Dark brown/black coloration
- Sunken, collapsed tissue
- Concentric ring-like patterning
- No visible mycelium/fuzzy growth

This is classic fruit rot with concentric zonation — strongly suggestive of **Anthracnose**. Let me confirm with one reference image.

The reference image shows Anthracnose conidia (microscopic spores) — confirming this is a Colletotrichum disease. The test image shows the macroscopic fruit symptom: large, sunken, dark lesions with concentric ring patterning on pepper fruit, which is the classic field presentation of Anthracnose caused by Colletotrichum species.

Key evidence:
- Large, sunken, dark brown-black lesions on fruit
- Concentric ring/zonation pattern within the lesions
- Fruit tissue collapsed and rotting
- No fuzzy mycelium (rules out Gray Mold, Sclerotinia)
- No white cottony growth (rules out Southern Blight)
